sides.text: A contract allows the customer to inspect a vendor's security controls. Which clause is this?
A. Right-to-audit

more.text: A right-to-audit clause permits inspection of the vendor.

sides.text: A team talks through a ransomware scenario in a meeting without touching any systems. Which test is this?
B. Tabletop exercise

more.text: A tabletop is a discussion-based walkthrough.

sides.text: A tool records process behavior on laptops and can isolate an infected one. Which is it?
B. EDR

more.text: EDR monitors endpoint behavior and enables response actions.

sides.text: A forum comment contains a script that steals other users' session cookies. Which attack is this?
A. Stored cross-site scripting

more.text: Script saved on the server and run in other users' browsers is stored XSS.

sides.text: Which appliance sits in front of internal servers, hiding them and distributing requests?
B. Reverse proxy

more.text: A reverse proxy fronts servers. A forward proxy fronts users.

sides.text: A retired server's drives are cryptographically erased so they can be reused. Which process is this?
D. Sanitization

more.text: Sanitization removes data while allowing media to be reused.

sides.text: Which term describes the risk that remains after controls are applied?
B. Residual risk

more.text: Inherent risk is before controls; residual is after.

sides.text: An employee signs up for an unapproved cloud storage service and stores customer files there. What is this?
D. Shadow IT

more.text: Shadow IT is technology used without IT's approval, creating blind spots.

sides.text: A company wants to enforce encryption and remote wipe on employee smartphones. Which solution fits?
D. MDM

more.text: Mobile device management enforces policy and remote wipe on phones.

sides.text: Which log source shows which device held a given IP address at a certain time?
A. DHCP or network logs

more.text: DHCP logs map IP addresses to devices over time.

sides.text: Data being processed in memory is in which state?
B. Data in use

more.text: In use means actively processed, such as in RAM.

sides.text: A company wants to avoid buying servers and pay only for what it uses. Which model fits?
B. Cloud computing

more.text: Cloud computing is on-demand and billed by usage.

sides.text: An attacker tries one or two common passwords against thousands of accounts to avoid lockouts. Which attack is this?
D. Password spraying

more.text: Spraying spreads a few guesses across many accounts to avoid lockout thresholds.

sides.text: A vendor processes payroll data only under a company's instructions. What is the vendor's role?
C. Processor

more.text: A processor acts on the controller's behalf.

sides.text: Which zero trust plane contains the policy enforcement point?
C. Data plane

more.text: The data plane enforces decisions. The control plane holds the policy engine and policy administrator.

sides.text: A user logs in once and opens several applications without re-entering credentials. Which is this?
A. SSO

more.text: Single sign-on authenticates once for many apps.

sides.text: A startup deliberately takes on high risk to grow quickly. Which risk appetite is this?
B. Expansionary

more.text: Expansionary appetite accepts more risk for growth.

sides.text: Which agreement sets standing terms for all future work orders?
D. MSA

more.text: An MSA covers general terms; each project then gets a SOW.

sides.text: An attacker copies a badge's data with a hidden reader and later enters with a duplicate. Which attack is this?
C. RFID cloning

more.text: RFID cloning duplicates a badge's credential.

sides.text: An asset worth $200,000 has an exposure factor of 25% and an ARO of 0.5. What is the ALE?
A user signs in from New York and then from Singapore ten minutes later. Which indicator is this?
D. Impossible travel

more.text: Logins too far apart in too little time suggest stolen credentials.

sides.text: Under GDPR, which role decides why personal data is collected?
C. Controller

more.text: The controller determines the purposes and means of processing.

sides.text: A company reviews a vendor's SOC 2 report prepared by an outside firm. What kind of evidence is this?
D. Independent assessment

more.text: An outside auditor's report is independent assurance.

sides.text: Which data should be collected first according to the order of volatility?
C. RAM

more.text: More volatile data is lost first, so RAM comes before disk.

sides.text: In a zero trust architecture, which component evaluates policy and context and decides whether to grant access?
A. Policy engine

more.text: The policy engine decides. The policy enforcement point carries out that decision on the data plane.

sides.text: Branch offices use low-cost internet links managed centrally by policy. Which technology is this?
D. SD-WAN

more.text: SD-WAN routes traffic over multiple links by policy with central management.

sides.text: A scan logs in to servers to check installed patches. Which type of scan is this?
A. Credentialed scan

more.text: Credentialed scans see patches and settings accurately.

sides.text: A gap analysis shows a company meets 70% of a framework's controls. What does this help with?
options: Prioritizing improvements toward the target standard

sides.text: C. Prioritizing improvements toward the target standard

more.text: Gap analysis compares the current state with a target and shows what must change.

sides.text: Which access control model decides based on attributes of the user, resource, and environment?
B. ABAC

more.text: ABAC evaluates multiple attributes against policy.

sides.text: Which incident response phase removes malware and closes the entry point?
C. Eradication

more.text: Eradication removes the cause. Containment only limits the spread.

sides.text: Which standard protects cardholder data and is enforced through card brands rather than law?
B. PCI DSS

more.text: PCI DSS is an industry standard for payment card security.

sides.text: A metric that warns risk is rising, such as the backlog of unpatched systems, is called a?
D. Key risk indicator

more.text: KRIs are measurable signals of increasing exposure.

sides.text: An unsupported operating system can't be updated and must stay online. What is the best compensating approach?
options: Isolate it on a restricted network segment
Leave it on the main network

sides.text: B. Isolate it on a restricted network segment

more.text: Isolation limits the exposure of a system that can't be patched.

sides.text: A SOAR playbook calls a firewall API to block an IP automatically. Which benefit does this show?
A. Faster reaction time

more.text: Automation responds in seconds. The other options are considerations, not benefits.

sides.text: Analysts search logs for signs of an attacker before any alert fires. Which activity is this?
B. Threat hunting

more.text: Threat hunting proactively looks for hidden compromise.

sides.text: Which document gives optional recommended practices?
C. Guideline

more.text: Guidelines advise without requiring. Policies and standards are mandatory.

sides.text: Which cookie flag stops JavaScript from reading a session cookie?
D. HttpOnly

more.text: HttpOnly blocks script access. Secure limits it to HTTPS.

sides.text: Which GDPR right lets individuals request deletion of their personal data?
D. Right to be forgotten

more.text: The right to erasure is commonly called the right to be forgotten.

sides.text: Malware spreads across the network on its own with no user action. Which type is it?
B. Worm

more.text: Worms self-replicate across networks. Viruses need a host file and user action.

sides.text: Which recovery site offers the fastest failover but costs the most?
A. Hot site

more.text: A hot site is fully equipped with current data.

sides.text: A critical system has no connection to any other network, including the internet. What is this called?
C. Air-gapped

more.text: An air gap is complete physical disconnection.

sides.text: Malicious code activates only after a specific employee's account is disabled. Which type is it?
A. Logic bomb

more.text: A logic bomb stays dormant until a condition is met.

sides.text: An attacker forces a connection to fall back to an older, weaker TLS version. Which attack is this?
D. Downgrade attack

more.text: A downgrade attack pushes systems to a weaker protocol.

sides.text: Users who mistype a company's domain land on a fake login page. Which attack is this?
D. Typosquatting

more.text: Typosquatting registers lookalike misspelled domains. DNS poisoning would redirect even correct entries.

sides.text: A call center agent sees only the last four digits of a card number. Which technique is this?
C. Masking

more.text: Masking hides parts of a value in display.

sides.text: A DNS record lists the mail servers allowed to send for a domain. Which email control is this?
C. SPF

more.text: SPF lists authorized sending servers.

sides.text: A user enters ' OR 1=1 -- into a login field and gains access. Which control best prevents this?
C. Parameterized queries

more.text: Parameterized queries keep input from being interpreted as SQL.

sides.text: A spreadsheet tracks identified risks with owners and treatments. What is it called?
C. Risk register

more.text: A risk register lists risks, owners, ratings, and treatments.

sides.text: Which BIA output states the maximum acceptable data loss, measured in time?
B. RPO

more.text: RPO limits data loss. RTO limits downtime.

sides.text: An attacker compromises a website that a target company's engineers frequently visit in order to infect them. Which attack is this?
C. Watering hole

more.text: A watering hole compromises a site the targets trust and visit.

sides.text: Which protocol lets an app access a user's resources through tokens without the password?
C. OAuth

more.text: OAuth delegates authorization with tokens.

sides.text: Employees choose a laptop from an approved list that the company owns. Which model is this?
D. CYOD

more.text: CYOD lets employees pick from approved company devices.

sides.text: A tiny spoofed DNS query produces a very large response aimed at a victim. Which technique is this?
B. Amplified DDoS

more.text: Amplification abuses a service so small requests generate large responses.

sides.text: Which provides integrity, authentication, and non-repudiation but not confidentiality?
D. Digital signature

more.text: A signature proves origin and unaltered content. It doesn't hide the message.

sides.text: Which authentication method is phishing-resistant and uses hardware with public-key cryptography?
D. FIDO2 security key

more.text: FIDO2 keys verify the site, so phishing doesn't work.

sides.text: A US firm must keep EU customer data inside the EU. Which concept applies?
D. Data sovereignty

more.text: Data is subject to the laws of where it's stored or processed.

sides.text: A device must authenticate through a RADIUS server before a switch port forwards traffic. Which standard is this?

more.text: 802.1X provides port-based network access control.

sides.text: A document lists the exact steps to configure a firewall. Which type is it?
A. Procedure

more.text: A procedure gives step-by-step instructions.

sides.text: Only approved executables may run on public kiosks. Which mitigation is in use?
A. Application allow list

more.text: An allow list blocks everything not explicitly approved.

sides.text: Admins receive elevated rights for two hours, after which the rights expire automatically. Which approach is this?
D. Just-in-time permissions

more.text: JIT grants temporary privilege and then revokes it.

sides.text: Which secure protocol and port replace Telnet?
A. SSH on port 22

more.text: SSH encrypts remote administration and uses port 22.

sides.text: A server runs unused services and still has default admin credentials. Which action addresses both problems?
C. Hardening

more.text: Hardening disables unneeded services and changes default credentials.

sides.text: A vendor can't patch quickly, so a WAF rule blocks exploitation in the meantime. What is this?
A. Compensating control

more.text: A WAF rule stands in for the missing patch.

sides.text: A web admin needs one certificate to cover mail.example.com and shop.example.com. Which type fits best?
B. Wildcard

more.text: A wildcard certificate (*.example.com) covers all subdomains of a domain.

sides.text: An email that appears to come from the CEO urgently asks finance to wire money to a new account. Which attack is this?
A. Business email compromise

more.text: BEC uses spoofed or hijacked executive email to trigger fraudulent payments.

sides.text: Management decides that fixing a low risk costs more than the possible loss and signs off. Which strategy is this?
D. Accept

more.text: Knowingly tolerating a risk is acceptance.

sides.text: A company buys cyber insurance. Which risk strategy is this?
A. Transfer

more.text: Insurance moves the financial impact to a third party.

sides.text: Which control category includes risk assessments and security policies written by senior leaders?
D. Managerial

more.text: Managerial controls govern and oversee risk. Technical controls are enforced by systems; operational ones are carried out by people.

sides.text: A phone's OS restrictions have been removed so unsigned apps can be installed. What is this called?
C. Jailbreaking

more.text: Jailbreaking removes the OS's built-in restrictions. Side loading installs apps from outside the store.

sides.text: A flaw has a CVSS score of 9.8. How is it rated?
C. Critical

more.text: CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 is Critical.

sides.text: An overlong input crashes a program and lets the attacker run code. Which vulnerability is this?
A. Buffer overflow

more.text: Input larger than the buffer overwrites adjacent memory, which can allow code execution.

sides.text: A payment processor replaces stored card numbers with random values and keeps the originals in a vault. Which technique is this?
D. Tokenization

more.text: Tokenization swaps data for tokens with the real value held in a vault. Masking only hides part of a displayed value.

sides.text: A penetration tester is given network diagrams and source code. Which type of test is this?
B. Known environment

more.text: Full information makes it a known environment (white box) test.

sides.text: Which firewall failure mode prioritizes security over availability?
D. Fail-closed

more.text: Fail-closed blocks traffic when the device fails.

sides.text: Which indicator most likely points to cryptomining malware on a server?
options: Sustained 100% CPU from an unknown process

sides.text: A. Sustained 100% CPU from an unknown process

more.text: Unexplained high resource use is a classic cryptomining sign.

sides.text: A device without current patches is placed on a restricted VLAN until it's fixed. Which technology is this?
C. NAC

more.text: NAC checks device posture before granting full access.

sides.text: Which statement best describes least privilege?
options: Granting only the access needed to do a job

sides.text: C. Granting only the access needed to do a job

more.text: Least privilege limits the damage from mistakes and compromise.

sides.text: A company labels data whose loss would halt operations. Which classification fits?
D. Critical

more.text: Critical data is essential to operations.

sides.text: Everyone who handled a hard drive signs a log. What is this called?
B. Chain of custody

more.text: Chain of custody documents who handled evidence and when.

sides.text: Which email control tells receivers to reject messages that fail SPF and DKIM alignment?
B. DMARC

more.text: DMARC sets the policy for authentication failures.

sides.text: Which tamper-resistant device is used to generate and store keys for servers and certificate authorities?
D. HSM

more.text: An HSM is dedicated hardware for key protection. A TPM is a chip on a single device's motherboard.

sides.text: A sensor receives a copy of traffic from a switch and can alert but not block. Which deployment is this?
A. Passive tap or monitor

more.text: A tap or monitor sees a copy of traffic and can't block it.

sides.text: Which Wi-Fi standard uses SAE to resist offline password cracking?
A. WPA3

more.text: WPA3 replaces the PSK handshake with SAE.

sides.text: Servers and networks are deployed from version-controlled templates. What is this called?
B. Infrastructure as code

more.text: IaC provisions infrastructure from machine-readable files.

sides.text: Which VPN setup sends only corporate-bound traffic through the tunnel?
C. Split tunnel

more.text: A split tunnel sends only designated traffic through the VPN.

sides.text: Which tool aggregates and correlates logs from many sources to alert on attacks?
D. SIEM

more.text: A SIEM centralizes and correlates security logs.

sides.text: A file's permissions are checked, then the file is swapped before it is opened. Which vulnerability is this?
A. Race condition (TOCTOU)

more.text: The state changed between the time of check and the time of use.

sides.text: A software update requires restarting a critical service. What should the change process include?
options: Scheduling the restart in a maintenance window with stakeholder notice

sides.text: A. Scheduling the restart in a maintenance window with stakeholder notice

more.text: Planning restarts and downtime is a technical implication of change management.

sides.text: A vulnerability scanner reports a flaw on a host that is already patched. What is this?
A. False positive

more.text: A false positive reports a problem that doesn't exist.

sides.text: A laptop is stolen. Which control best keeps the data on its drive unreadable?
D. Full-disk encryption

more.text: Full-disk encryption protects data at rest on a lost device.
